napa-sonoma.title: Best Luxury Hotels in Napa Valley, Ranked | Suites With Keith
napa-sonoma.description: Keith's firsthand ranking of the best luxury hotels in Napa Valley and Sonoma, from personal stays over several years — honeymoons, wine weekends, and family escapes.
napa-sonoma.h1: Best Luxury Hotels in Napa Valley & Sonoma, Ranked
napa-sonoma.tagline: After personally staying at nearly every luxury hotel in wine country, here's exactly where I'd spend my own money.
intro_paras: Most "best hotel" lists are compiled from online reviews or press materials. This one isn't.

Over the past several years, I've personally stayed at nearly every luxury hotel in Napa & Sonoma — every ranking below reflects my own experience, both as a luxury travel advisor and as a frequent visitor to wine country.
Whether you're planning a honeymoon, anniversary, girls' getaway, or long weekend, this guide is designed to help you choose the hotel that's actually right for your trip.

cards.name: Meadowood Napa Valley
cards.bestfor: Perfect For · Honeymoons, Celebrations, Wine Lovers, Returning Visitors
cards.desc: There's something so special about Meadowood, and it's sort of hard to put your finger on it. Service is at Aman quality standards, with a real sense of place, spacious and fairly private cottages, a beautiful spa, and thoughtful turndown treats each evening. It's a small property — around 40 cottages — and there really isn't a bad room to be had.

notes.b: Mind the stairs.
notes.t: About 90% of rooms aren't fully accessible, though buggies are available for those with mobility concerns.

notes.b: It skews a bit older.
notes.t: The property tends to attract 40+ couples, though there's a family pool and it works well solo too.

notes.b: The tennis facility is a hidden gem.
notes.t: Beautiful courts with instructors I'd recommend in a heartbeat.

cards.perks_label: Fora / Virtuoso Preferred Partner Benefits Apply
cards.perks_items: Often includes an additional $500 credit
cards.take: Every time I go to Meadowood, I feel well taken care of — and I can't say that about every property on this list.

cards.name: Four Seasons Napa Valley
cards.bestfor: Perfect For · Families, Girls Trips, Couples, Groups
cards.desc: I've stayed at Four Seasons four or five times now, and since they've worked out the early kinks, I think they've earned the #2 spot. Architecturally the hotel is beautiful, with a mix of dark, moody rooms and bright white farmhouse styles set within the vineyards. The pools are gorgeous, the 1-star Michelin restaurant is fantastic, and I love the pool bar.

notes.b: Service is Four Seasons standard.
notes.t: This is genuinely what separates it from the property just below it on this list.

notes.b: Request an upper floor if shower privacy matters.
notes.t: Some ground-floor outdoor showers face the pathways — easily handled at booking.

notes.b: It fits a huge range of travelers.
notes.t: Families, couples, girls trips, and multi-couple groups all work well here.

cards.perks_label: Fora / Virtuoso Preferred Partner Benefits Apply
cards.perks_items: Sometimes includes a 3rd or 4th night free
cards.take: It's a great property that lends itself to a large swath of people.

cards.name: Montage Healdsburg
cards.bestfor: Perfect For · Wine Lovers, Couples, Returning Visitors
cards.desc: I love the Montage and have stayed there at least 20 times over the past few years. It's perfectly situated just outside downtown Healdsburg, close to wineries, with a complimentary shuttle to the plaza. The dining has perhaps the best view of any restaurant on this list, and I actually prefer the vineyard rooms over the mountain or oak rooms.

notes.b: Book a vineyard room.
notes.t: Waking up and sitting by your fire pit overlooking the vineyards never gets old.

notes.b: Twenty stays in, I notice the small things.
notes.t: A few more little misses lately than in year one — nothing that moves it from my top three, and the team always makes it right.

notes.b: They remember you.
notes.t: One masseuse in particular I make a point to see every time I go.

cards.perks_label: Fora / Virtuoso Preferred Partner Benefits Apply
cards.perks_items: Sometimes includes a 3rd or 4th night free
cards.take: It's just a great property, and I feel lucky I've spent so many nights there.

cards.name: Solage Calistoga
cards.bestfor: Perfect For · Younger Couples, Families, Girls Trips
cards.desc: Solage is sort of iconic and really defines California wine country luxury. It lands just outside my top three mostly on polish — the experience is intentionally more relaxed than white-glove, and the spa, a signature here, is due some love. That said, I love the design, and most rooms have a private garden or terrace, some with private hot tubs.

notes.b: Great for full privacy.
notes.t: If you need a completely private terrace, Solage is one of the best options on this list.

notes.b: Set spa expectations.
notes.t: The spa is a big part of the Solage story and is due for a refresh — worth knowing as you plan treatments.

notes.b: Rates run lower than the properties above.
notes.t: A strong cost-to-experience option in Calistoga.

cards.perks_label: Fora / Virtuoso Preferred Partner Benefits Apply
cards.perks_items: Sometimes includes a 3rd or 4th night free
cards.take: A fantastic hotel — just not quite at the level of the three above it.

cards.name: MacArthur Place
cards.bestfor: Perfect For · Returning Visitors, Walkability, Wine Tasting
cards.desc: I love MacArthur Place and think it's such a hidden gem in Sonoma. It's right next to downtown, so you can walk or bike into town, the design is beautiful, prices are reasonable, and the pool just finished an extensive remodel. It's also just an easy getaway from San Francisco.

notes.b: Easiest walk to town on this list.
notes.t: No worrying about driving back after a few glasses of wine.

notes.b: Wellness is modest here.
notes.t: The draw is the gardens, the remodeled pool, and the town itself.

notes.b: Downtown Sonoma itself is a big draw.
notes.t: Quaint, local, and less commercialized than Healdsburg, with easy access to Glen Ellen.

cards.perks_label: Fora / Virtuoso Preferred Partner Benefits Apply
cards.take: A great option for return visitors who'd rather not drive back to their hotel every night.

cards.name: Stanly Ranch
cards.tag: Beautiful, But Not Quite Wine Country
cards.bestfor: Perfect For · Younger Couples, Wellness Travelers, Design Lovers
cards.desc: Stanly Ranch might be the most architecturally striking hotel on this list. The spa is arguably the prettiest here, every room has a large outdoor terrace with a fire pit, and Bear, the main restaurant, is one of the more interesting dining options in Napa.

notes.b: The location doesn't quite deliver the classic wine country feeling.
notes.t: It's convenient to both Napa and Sonoma, but sits out in the marshes.

notes.b: Terrace privacy varies.
notes.t: Some are wonderfully secluded, others more open — I'll steer you to the best-sited rooms.

notes.b: The smart-room tech takes a night.
notes.t: Give the lighting controls an evening to learn — after that you're fluent.

cards.perks_label: Fora / Virtuoso Preferred Partner Benefits Apply
cards.perks_items: Sometimes includes a 3rd or 4th night free
cards.take: Beautiful, but I don't find myself wanting to go back as often as the hotels above it.

cards.name: Madrona Manor
cards.bestfor: Perfect For · Couples, Romantic Getaways
cards.desc: Madrona Manor feels completely different from every other hotel on this list — more like staying at someone's incredibly beautiful estate than a traditional luxury hotel. The design by Jay Jeffers is stunning, and sitting on the front porch with a glass of wine overlooking the vineyards is one of my favorite experiences anywhere in Sonoma County.

notes.b: No spa, and the pool is underwhelming.
notes.t: The main drawbacks on an otherwise special property.

notes.b: Hop on an e-bike into Healdsburg Plaza.
notes.t: Just a few minutes away, while the property itself stays peaceful.

notes.b: This is a couples property.
notes.t: I wouldn't recommend it for families.

cards.perks_label: Fora / Virtuoso Preferred Partner Benefits Apply
cards.take: An easy recommendation for a romantic weekend with beautiful design and one of the most charming atmospheres in wine country.

cards.name: Carneros Resort & Spa
cards.bestfor: Perfect For · Families, Multi-Couple Groups, Older Couples
cards.desc: Carneros has the potential to be a top-five property on this list — a beloved classic ready for its next chapter. The grounds are sprawling and beautiful, every cottage has private outdoor space, and I actually prefer the location to Stanly Ranch — it feels much more like wine country.

notes.b: The spa is one of the larger in Napa Valley.
notes.t: And, like the rooms, it will shine brightest after a refresh.

notes.b: Consistency varies.
notes.t: Some stays have been flawless, others less so — I set expectations and pull strings accordingly.

notes.b: The two-bedroom residences are fantastic.
notes.t: I can't personally speak to the standard rooms, though most have private patios.

cards.perks_label: Fora / Virtuoso Preferred Partner Benefits Apply
cards.perks_items: Sometimes includes a 3rd or 4th night free
cards.take: With a renovation, I honestly think this property could move several spots higher on this list.

cards.name: Alila Napa Valley
cards.tag: A Great Hotel, Not Quite Wine Country
cards.bestfor: Perfect For · Modern Design Lovers, Younger Travelers
cards.desc: I like Alila quite a bit. Its personality is contemporary-first rather than vineyard-romantic — a genuinely lovely modern hotel whose aesthetic clicks instantly for some travelers. The location is excellent, and being able to walk into downtown St. Helena is a huge plus.

notes.b: Book a vineyard-facing room.
notes.t: Significantly better than the alternatives if you can get one.

notes.b: The pool is intimate rather than resort-scale.
notes.t: Plan big pool days elsewhere and use Alila as your stylish, walkable base.

notes.b: You can walk to dinner.
notes.t: Downtown St. Helena is a few minutes on foot — rare enough in the valley to matter.

cards.perks_label: Fora / Virtuoso Preferred Partner Benefits Apply
cards.take: A good hotel whose modern character is a matter of taste — my ranking reflects my preference for vineyard romance more than any flaw in execution.

best-hotels-greece.title: The 10 Best Luxury Hotels in Greece & the Greek Islands | Suites With Keith
best-hotels-greece.description: After four weeks in Greece and 38 hotel visits across seven islands, here are Keith's 10 favorite luxury hotels — plus smart island pairings and how to move between them.
best-hotels-greece.h1: The 10 Best Luxury Hotels in Greece & the Greek Islands
best-hotels-greece.tagline: After four weeks traveling through Greece and visiting 38 hotels across seven islands, these are the ten I'd send my clients to first.
intro_paras: After spending four weeks traveling through Greece and visiting 38 hotels across seven islands, I came away with a very different perspective on the Greek luxury hotel landscape.

I've previously ranked my favorite honeymoon hotels in Santorini and shared island-by-island picks throughout The Collections, but after staying at and touring this many properties, I wanted to put together a definitive list of my 10 favorite luxury hotels in Greece.

This isn't meant to be an absolute ranking of every luxury hotel in the country — I didn't visit Crete or One&Only Kea on this trip, for example. But having personally experienced this many properties across the Cyclades, I have a pretty comprehensive perspective on what actually distinguishes the best hotels in Greece. And, perhaps more importantly: the most expensive hotel isn't necessarily the best hotel. Location, design, privacy, service, food, wellness facilities, room quality, and the overall sense of place all played a role in these rankings.

Booking through me includes Fora preferred partner amenities — think space-available upgrades, daily breakfast, and hotel credits — on top of the personal relationships I built with the teams at these properties, who I trust to take extra care of my clients. Rates through me are identical to booking direct — the perks are not.

cards.name: Canaves Epitome · Santorini
cards.tag: The Single Best Hotel I Experienced In Greece
cards.bestfor: Perfect For · Return Visitors, Families, Privacy Seekers, Design Lovers
cards.desc: Wow, I don't really know what to say about Epitome, other than wow. This was my favorite hotel across nine islands in the Cyclades, and perhaps one of the top three stays of my entire life. The one thing to understand: it sits a short walk from Oia near Ammoudi Bay rather than directly on the Caldera — so first-time visitors picturing the classic cliffside image are choosing a different experience. For me, that tradeoff is more than worth it. Landscaped gardens behind volcanic-rock walls make the common areas feel a world away from the busy streets of Oia, and with 53 rooms and no age restrictions, it still feels boutique.

notes.b: The two-bedroom suites are the star.
notes.t: Separated by floor with large pools, decks, and outdoor dining areas — some rooms sit below the pool with views looking up into it.

notes.b: The best sunset in Greece.
notes.t: You're watching an actual sunset into the Aegean rather than watching the sun disappear behind the Caldera.

notes.b: Omnia was the best hotel restaurant I ate at all trip.
notes.t: And full-property buyouts are available — though for a dedicated villa buyout, Canaves Sunday is my pick for the best villa in Santorini.

cards.perks_items: Upgrade on arrival (space available) · Daily breakfast · Hotel credit
cards.take: If you're asking me for the single best hotel I experienced across the Greek islands on this trip — it's Canaves Epitome.

cards.name: Gundari · Folegandros
cards.bestfor: Perfect For · Honeymoons, Anniversaries, Remote Luxury Seekers
cards.desc: You get picked up at the port — or helicopter charter directly in — and after a short drive, you hit a dirt road out toward the cliff's edge. In the distance, a beautiful dark stone building blends into the horizon. It's unlike anything I've ever seen. Gundari has 27 suites and villas, all with endless ocean views and private plunge pools, and because Folegandros sits on a somewhat obscure ferry line, the people who are there really want to be there — quiet, like-minded, and laid back. Every little design detail here was clearly very well thought out, down to the outdoor shower overlooking the Aegean.

notes.b: The coolest infinity pool in the Cyclades.
notes.t: Without a doubt — and the spa and gym were fantastic as well.

notes.b: Give it three nights.
notes.t: If it's booked out and you can only do two, still go — Folegandros is right next to Santorini, so it's an easy honeymoon or anniversary add-on.

notes.b: A team that listens.
notes.t: When guests flag anything at all, the staff responds with genuine gratitude and speed — the kind of ownership mentality you hope for at this level.

cards.perks_items: Upgrade on arrival (space available) · Daily breakfast · Hotel credit
cards.take: Folegandros is a fantastic island, and Gundari makes it even more special.

cards.name: Canaves Oia Suites · Santorini
cards.bestfor: Perfect For · First-Time Visitors, Honeymooners, 40+ Couples
cards.desc: This was the best hotel I saw for first-time visitors to Santorini, and I'd be hard pressed to recommend any other hotel first if someone specifically wants the classic caldera-luxury experience. Recently completely renovated, it blew me away everywhere I looked: quality of finishes, privacy (a rarity on Santorini), private water features, and landscaping. It's set higher on the Caldera than most, so you get more privacy, and every room has coverings above the outdoor spaces.

notes.b: The River Pool Suite is the single best suite I saw in Greece.
notes.t: Across all 38 hotels.

notes.b: 46 total suites and villas.
notes.t: Including private two- and three-bedroom pool villas — a rarity in Oia or Imerovigli.

notes.b: The best spa product on the Caldera.
notes.t: Completely brand new, plus a large gym and easy shuttle access to the other Canaves properties. Note the 13+ age requirement.

cards.perks_items: Upgrade on arrival (space available) · Daily breakfast · €100 hotel credit
cards.take: For first-timers, honeymooners, and 40+ couples who want the classic Santorini experience, this is the one. See how every hotel on the island stacks up in my full Santorini ranking.

cards.name: Parilio · Paros
cards.bestfor: Perfect For · Design Lovers, Couples, Families & Groups In The Villas
cards.desc: As a design lover, Parilio was perhaps my favorite stay in the Cyclades. It's set just outside Naoussa, and while most rooms don't have ocean views, it doesn't really matter — the property itself is so beautiful, and the way the light moves through it around twilight is magical. What I loved most, though, was the service: the staff actually cared to get to know you and your preferences. The food was fantastic, the massage was great, and as a bonus, guests can use the beach club at sister property Cosme for free.

notes.b: Request the Sun Suite up at the villas.
notes.t: One of the three Sun Suites sits at the new hilltop villas with ocean views and a massive private pool — ask for that specific one.

notes.b: The new villas are a sneaky value.
notes.t: Three-bedroom villas run around $3,000–$3,500 per night in peak season — brand new, with full access to the hotel's amenities. For a group or family, that's genuinely reasonable.

notes.b: Expect kids at the pool in July.
notes.t: It was quiet during my stay, but peak-summer guests told me otherwise. That's Paros in July.

cards.perks_items: Upgrade on arrival (space available) · Daily breakfast · Hotel credit
cards.take: I'm very pro private-villas-at-hotels these days versus standalone villas — and Parilio's are the best case for it. Torn between here and Cosme? My full comparison settles it.

cards.name: Andronis Boutique · Santorini
cards.bestfor: Perfect For · Younger Honeymooners, First-Time Visitors
cards.desc: Andronis Boutique is a truly fantastic, top-notch hotel — firmly in the very top tier of my Santorini list. Recently renovated, the rooms are authentic cave-style rooms with beautiful finishes and fixtures, and some of the suites are incredibly unique, particularly the two-level Eternal Suite. Every room has a plunge pool or jacuzzi — which isn't the case at the Canaves hotels — and rates tend to land slightly below sister property Andronis Luxury Suites.

notes.b: The "stay in Imerovigli to avoid crowds" narrative doesn't hold here.
notes.t: At the top Oia properties, no one is walking directly in front of your room — while several Imerovigli hotels sit right on the Fira-to-Oia hiking path. If privacy matters, say so when booking.

notes.b: Spa devotees should also look at Andronis Concept.
notes.t: Its spa in Imerovigli was one of my top five in the Cyclades.

notes.b: For a honeymoon, compare the top tier.
notes.t: Andronis Boutique, Andronis Luxury Suites, Canaves Ena, and Canaves Oia Suites — judged on the actual room, privacy, water feature, and price. Between those, you really can't go wrong — my Santorini ranking compares them all.

cards.perks_items: Upgrade on arrival (space available) · Daily breakfast · €100 hotel credit
cards.take: Cave-style rooms are what people picture when they book Santorini — and Boutique's are the real thing.

cards.name: Bill & Coo Coast · Mykonos
cards.bestfor: Perfect For · Couples, Beach Club Lovers, Long Lunches
cards.desc: I stayed at Bill & Coo's Mykonos Town property, but I preferred the Coast location for a few reasons: it's adults-only, it has a beautiful private beach club, rooms sit directly on the ocean, and the suites are massive and incredibly private — some with truly spectacular private pools. The Coast location also sits in a protected bay, so the meltemi winds that can whip the Town property's infinity pool are far more minimal here. If I had the choice, I'd always choose Coast.

notes.b: The best breakfasts I had in Greece.
notes.t: At any hotel, on any island. I was usually full until dinner.

notes.b: A massive new gym complex and spa are underway.
notes.t: Once completed, they should bring the property to another level.

notes.b: Independently owned, with staff who return season after season.
notes.t: To me, that's one of the best signs that things work well behind the scenes. Lunch at Beefbar is a bit sceney, but the beach club itself is extremely relaxing.

cards.perks_items: Upgrade on arrival (space available) · Daily breakfast · Hotel credit
cards.take: Like Cali and Kalesma, Bill & Coo proves how good Greece's independent hotels are at creating a real sense of place.

cards.name: Kalesma · Mykonos
cards.bestfor: Perfect For · Couples, Sunset Lovers, Slow Evenings In
cards.desc: Wow, Kalesma is such a beautiful property. The combination of Cycladic minimalism with dark woods and marble just works incredibly well, and the location is fantastic — set above Ornos Bay and very central on Mykonos. It's very much a couples-oriented property; children are allowed, but I didn't see any during my two nights. I loved sitting in my jacuzzi with a glass of wine overlooking the bay so much that one night I skipped going out entirely and had dinner on my own patio.

notes.b: Request the junior suites left of the pool bar.
notes.t: They're more private than the one I stayed in — and interestingly, the base rooms above the junior suites are more private still.

notes.b: The fire pit overlooking Delos.
notes.t: A fantastic place to sit around sunset before heading out to dinner.

notes.b: Wellness is intimate, not the headline.
notes.t: The spa is small and the gym covers the basics — come for the design, the views, and the calm.

cards.perks_items: Upgrade on arrival (space available) · Daily breakfast · Hotel credit
cards.take: Cali is flashier on paper, but Kalesma's laid-back beauty is what won me over.

cards.name: Cali · Mykonos
cards.tag: The Best Hotel Gym I've Ever Seen
cards.bestfor: Perfect For · Fitness-Minded Travelers, Privacy Seekers
cards.desc: I really loved Cali and think it's such a unique offering on Mykonos. Located on the island's quieter eastern side, it's another of Greece's incredible independent hotels with a strong sense of place — something I often find lacking at the big luxury brands. Service was extremely refined, with staff calling guests by name and anticipating needs, and the infinity pool is one of the largest and most unique I saw in Greece, with real space between loungers. Many rooms have private plunge pools that are very, very private — a genuine rarity in Greece.

notes.b: The gym is genuinely remarkable.
notes.t: Pilates reformers, squat racks, dumbbells up to 75 pounds, plus padel, tennis, and pickleball. I'd stay here again just for the gym.

notes.b: Far from the party scene — by design.
notes.t: But the hotel can arrange boat or car transfers to the beach clubs and nightclubs if that's what you're after.

notes.b: Mykonos is a smart entry point.
notes.t: It's easy to reach from Europe and the Middle East — fly in, move south through the Cyclades, and save Athens for a separate trip.

cards.perks_items: Upgrade on arrival (space available) · Daily breakfast · Hotel credit
cards.take: A somewhat American, almost LA-like feel — but a genuinely remarkable property I'd happily return to.

cards.name: Cosme · Paros
cards.bestfor: Perfect For · Couples, Families With Teens, 4-Night Stays
cards.desc: I loved Cosme. The laid-back luxury beach vibe is really refreshing, and while the room rates are high, the base rooms are massive — larger than many hotels' junior suites. The service was refined, the dining was fantastic, and the location is hard to beat on Paros: walking distance to Naoussa with a private beach club directly in front of the hotel. And despite what you may have heard, Paros is not "the new Mykonos" — Naoussa is lively and fun without the flashy scene. It's honestly just a really easy, nicely rounded Greek island.

notes.b: Skip the plunge-pool rooms overlooking the shared pool.
notes.t: The top categories have ocean-view plunge pools, but they're not particularly private — I'd opt for a suite set farther back on the property.

notes.b: The circular spa and gym buildings are a highlight.
notes.t: Between those, the beach club, and the dining, you could comfortably spend four nights without getting bored.

notes.b: Shoulder season is the play.
notes.t: In May or September/October, rates can drop dramatically from peak summer pricing.

cards.perks_items: Upgrade on arrival (space available) · Daily breakfast · Hotel credit
cards.take: Deciding between Paros's two best? Read my full Cosme vs. Parilio comparison.

cards.name: Stamna · Sifnos
cards.tag: Design-Forward Calm On Greece's Great Foodie Island
cards.bestfor: Perfect For · Slow Travelers, Foodies, Design-Conscious Couples
cards.desc: After ten nights between Mykonos and Paros, arriving at Stamna after a somewhat brutal ferry ride was a fantastic respite. Set above some of Sifnos's best beaches and centrally located in Apollonia, it's a small, design-forward hotel with excellent dining on what's known as one of Greece's great foodie islands. The design is earthy, neutral, and calming, with a wonderful feeling of being perched above the Cyclades — views stretching as far as you can see — and service that's warm and casual but still solid.

notes.b: Sifnos rewards slow travel.
notes.t: It's one of my favorite Greek islands for hiking, food, and its rugged mountainous landscape — and Stamna is the pick if you want a smaller, design-conscious hotel over a big resort.

notes.b: No spa or gym that I could find.
notes.t: And the pool draws a mix of young families and honeymooners, so it isn't always as relaxing as you'd expect.

notes.b: The $25-per-bag laundry service is a quiet hero.
notes.t: You can fit a surprising amount in one bag — a lifesaver when you're doing four weeks in Greece with only a carry-on.

cards.perks_items: Upgrade on arrival (space available) · Daily breakfast · Hotel credit
cards.take: Small, calm, and perched above the Cyclades — exactly what you want Sifnos to be.

pairings.a: Mykonos → Santorini — fly into Mykonos, ferry south, save Athens for another trip
Mykonos → Milos → Santorini — Sarakiniko and sea caves between the icons
Parilio's villas on Paros + Canaves Epitome (no age limits)
Folegandros + Paros — the quiet side of the Cyclades
May or September–October — same hotels, dramatically better pricing

cards.name: Canaves Oia Suites
cards.tag: The Best Hotel On The Island
cards.bestfor: Perfect For · First-Time Visitors, Honeymoons, 40+ Couples
cards.desc: For first-time visitors to Santorini, I'd be hard pressed to recommend any other hotel first. Perched high on the Caldera, Canaves Oia Suites was recently completely renovated and blew me away everywhere I looked — the quality of finishes, the privacy (a rarity on Santorini), the private water features, and the landscaping. Set higher on the Caldera than most, you get more privacy, and every room has coverings above the outdoor spaces.

notes.b: Best spa product on the Caldera.
notes.t: Completely brand new, plus a large gym and easy shuttle access to other Canaves properties.

notes.b: 46 total suites and villas.
notes.t: Including private 2-3 bedroom pool villas — a rarity in Oia or Imerovigli.

notes.b: Not for everyone.
notes.t: There's a 13+ age requirement, and complete privacy simply doesn't exist anywhere on the Caldera.

cards.perks_items: Upgrade on arrival (space available) · Daily breakfast · €100 hotel credit
cards.take: There's a reason this is the flagship of the Canaves portfolio, and a reason it's the best hotel on the island.

cards.name: Andronis Boutique Hotel
cards.bestfor: Perfect For · First-Time Visitors, Younger Couples
cards.desc: Andronis Boutique is a perfect offering for first-time Santorini visitors — and it runs the very top of this list incredibly close. Rooms were all renovated in 2024 and are pristine, cave-style rooms with some incredibly unique layouts. Set lower on the Caldera than Oia Suites, there's slightly less privacy, but the property still has coverings over private patios and the rooms felt surprisingly bright for cave-style rooms.

notes.b: This is what people picture.
notes.t: If you're coming to Santorini for the first time, cave-style rooms are what you're expecting, and Boutique offers some of the best on the island.

notes.b: Just 25 suites & villas.
notes.t: Feels intimate but still very private, and priced slightly below Andronis Luxury Suites.

notes.b: Book dinner at Lycabettus immediately.
notes.t: Reserve as soon as you book your room — it's Andronis' famous cliffside restaurant.

cards.perks_items: Upgrade on arrival (space available) · Daily breakfast · €100 hotel credit
cards.take: I loved the finishes here — lots of marble with beautiful wooden arches, very similar to Oia Suites.

cards.name: Canaves Epitome
cards.bestfor: Perfect For · Couples, Privacy Seekers, Design Lovers, Families
cards.desc: This may surprise some, but Canaves Epitome makes an excellent case for being the #1 hotel on Santorini — the only drawback (or benefit, depending on preference) is the location, a short walk from Oia near Ammoudi Bay. If you're returning to Santorini, traveling as a family, or want complete privacy and an actual sunset into the Aegean, this is the best hotel for you.

notes.b: The gardens feel like a world away.
notes.t: Landscaping behind volcanic-rock walls makes the common areas feel magical and far from the busy streets.

notes.b: The 2-bedroom suites are the star.
notes.t: Separated by floor with large pools, decks, and outdoor dining — some rooms even sit below the pool with views up into it.

notes.b: Just 53 rooms, no age restrictions.
notes.t: Still boutique in feel despite being more spread out than the Caldera hotels.

cards.perks_items: Upgrade on arrival (space available) · Daily breakfast · €100 hotel credit
cards.take: I have to say, Canaves Epitome was my favorite hotel across 9 islands in the Cyclades, and perhaps one of the top 3 stays of my entire life.

cards.name: Andronis Luxury Suites
cards.bestfor: Perfect For · 50+ Couples, Anniversary Trips, Mobility-Conscious Travelers
cards.desc: The flagship of the Andronis portfolio is every bit as beautiful as its younger sibling, Andronis Boutique — more exclusive on paper, refined and elegant, with a classic old-school luxury character rather than cave-style Santorini. It lends itself well to a 50+ clientele on anniversary trips or returning for the first time since their honeymoon.

notes.b: Good for mobility concerns.
notes.t: A few suites near check-in have only 15-20 stairs — no need to trek hundreds of stairs to reach your room.

notes.b: Book Lycabettus immediately.
notes.t: Andronis' famous cliffside restaurant is located here — reserve as soon as you book.

notes.b: 39 total rooms, all spacious.
notes.t: Every room has a water feature — plunge pool, jacuzzi, or full pool in the villas.

cards.perks_items: Upgrade on arrival (space available) · Daily breakfast · €100 hotel credit
cards.take: Refined and unique in its own right, just slightly less 'authentic Santorini' than Boutique.

cards.name: Canaves Ena
cards.tag: The OG Of The Canaves Portfolio
cards.bestfor: Perfect For · Value Seekers, Social Travelers
cards.desc: Started in the 80s by the same family running it today, Ena is a little more minimalist than its younger siblings, and the size — just 18 suites — makes it feel very intimate. A 2024 renovation brought it up to date beautifully. Rooms are slightly smaller than Oia Suites, and not every room has a water feature like Andronis properties do.

notes.b: The swim-up bar is a highlight.
notes.t: A fun social addition on an island where couples tend to keep to themselves.

notes.b: Sits higher on the Caldera.
notes.t: Like Oia Suites, that means more privacy than other Caldera offerings.

notes.b: Rates are close to Andronis Boutique.
notes.t: Despite being positioned as the value option, I find the pricing almost always lands the same.

cards.perks_items: Upgrade on arrival (space available) · Daily breakfast · €100 hotel credit
cards.take: The team here, especially longtime sales director Des, is a big reason I trust sending clients to this property.

cards.name: Andronis Concept
cards.bestfor: Perfect For · Wellness Travelers, 4+ Night Stays, Design Lovers
cards.desc: Set near, but not in, Imerovigli, Concept is genuinely different from the rest of this list. It has the nicest spa I saw on Santorini — maybe in the Cyclades. Rooms are generous, feel very private, and the architecture breaks from the traditional white cave look with warm, earthy modern tones that blend into the volcanic landscape.

notes.b: Some rooms sit on the walking path.
notes.t: Not all, but a few have the Fira-to-Oia trail passing right in front — worth checking before booking.

notes.b: Just 28 suites and villas.
notes.t: Still feels boutique despite having some of the island's best wellness facilities.

notes.b: Andronis steers families toward Arcadia instead.
notes.t: Concept is family-friendly, but Arcadia's resort feel is the better fit for that group.

cards.perks_items: Upgrade on arrival (space available) · Daily breakfast · €100 hotel credit
cards.take: If this property were located in Oia instead, it'd probably be competing for one of my top three spots.

cards.name: Grace Hotel
cards.bestfor: Perfect For · Honeymooners Comfortable Outside Oia
cards.desc: Grace gets a lot right. Set way up on the Caldera in Imerovigli, you're sometimes literally above the fog line — a genuinely unique feeling, and ideal for honeymooners okay with being outside Oia. The room design is simple, white, and elegant, and surprisingly bright for Santorini.

notes.b: Room selection matters here.
notes.t: Some rooms sit along the Fira-to-Oia walking path — book through me and I'll make sure yours is one of the secluded ones.

notes.b: Choose the outdoor water features.
notes.t: Between the top categories, I'd guide clients to the outdoor plunge-pool rooms over the indoor hot tub suites.

notes.b: Dining is exceptional.
notes.t: Michelin-starred chef Lefteris Lazarou personally visits tables, and the food felt distinctly Greek yet modern.

cards.perks_items: Upgrade on arrival (space available) · Daily breakfast · €100 hotel credit
cards.take: A fantastic property — at current rates I usually find stronger value elsewhere on the island, but when pricing aligns, Grace absolutely belongs in the conversation.

cards.name: Andronis Arcadia
cards.bestfor: Perfect For · Families, Younger Couples, Scene-Seekers
cards.desc: Fantastic in theory, but not quite for me — Arcadia has Pacman and Beefbar on property, two very Mykonos-esque dining options that bring in a different vibe and clientele than the rest of this list. The location is similar to Canaves Epitome, right next door, with beautiful sunset-facing rooms and very private layouts.

notes.b: It's massive and spread out.
notes.t: You'll want a golf cart to get around in summer heat if there's no Meltemi wind.

notes.b: 114 rooms, resort-style feel.
notes.t: This reads more as a true resort than a boutique hotel — great for families.

notes.b: All rooms have private pools.
notes.t: Including some of the largest on the island.

cards.perks_items: Upgrade on arrival (space available) · Daily breakfast · €100 hotel credit
cards.take: Great if you like a bit of a scene; not the move if you want exclusivity and quiet.

cards.name: Mystique
cards.bestfor: Perfect For · A Prime Caldera Perch, Moody Minimalism
cards.desc: Mystique didn't connect with me the way the top of this list did — which surprised me, given how much I love the Empiria Group team behind some of the best hotels in the Cyclades. The rooms offer limited privacy, and the minimalist interiors read sparse to me — a setting this special deserves finishes to match.

notes.b: The setting is the strongest thing about it.
notes.t: A genuinely prime caldera position — better, right now, than the finishes inside it.

notes.b: The cave rooms run dark and quiet.
notes.t: Signature Mystique — wonderfully moody for some travelers, spare for others.

notes.b: The potential is obvious.
notes.t: The bones and location are genuinely good — with updated interiors, it competes at the very top.

cards.perks_items: Upgrade on arrival (space available) · Daily breakfast · €100 hotel credit
cards.take: For now I tend to guide clients a notch up this list — and I'd revisit it the moment the interiors catch up to the setting.

cards.name: Katikies Portfolio (3 Hotels)
cards.bestfor: Perfect For · Katikies Loyalists — And Everyone Else After The Refresh
cards.desc: Katikies holds some of the most storied real estate on Santorini — the setting across all 3 Caldera properties is undeniably beautiful, and the spa at Pelagos House is expansive and impressive. Where the portfolio trails the top of this list is simple: the interiors haven't kept pace with the island's recent renovation wave.

notes.b: No coverings over the patios.
notes.t: That lends itself to an overall lack of privacy compared to Andronis or Canaves.

notes.b: The interiors are classic rather than current.
notes.t: A furniture and finishes update would transform the experience.

notes.b: There's real potential here.
notes.t: If Katikies follows Andronis and Canaves in continuous renovation, these locations compete with anything on the island.

cards.perks_items: Upgrade on arrival (space available) · Daily breakfast · €100 hotel credit
cards.take: For now, my clients usually find the stronger value a notch up this list — and I'll be first in line to re-review the moment a refresh lands.
